cards.front: How do you calculate the [[kw:taxable amount]] when a trade discount is given?
back: $$\text{Taxable Amount} = \text{Selling Price} - \text{Trade Discounts}$$
Trade discounts are subtracted before calculating sales tax.
Cash discounts are taken after tax, not before.

cards.front: What is the formula for [[kw:sales tax]]?
back: $$\text{Sales Tax} = \text{Taxable Amount} \times \text{Sales Tax Rate}$$
Shipping charges are added after tax, not included in taxable amount.
Total cost = Taxable amount + Sales tax + Shipping.

cards.front: A battery sells for $32 with a $10.50 trade discount and 5% sales tax. Find the total cost before shipping.
back: Total before shipping = $21.50 + $1.08 = $22.58.
Cash discounts are calculated on the taxable amount only, never on tax or shipping.
They are subtracted after tax is calculated: Net = (Taxable + Tax + Shipping) – Cash discount.
[[imp:Cash discounts do NOT reduce the sales tax owed.]]

back: $$\text{Actual Sales} = \frac{\text{Total Sales (including tax)}}{1 + \text{Tax Rate}}$$
Sales Tax = Total Sales – Actual Sales.
The store keeps actual sales; the rest goes to the government.

What is [[kw:assessed value]] and how is it calculated?
back: A percentage of the property's market value used for tax purposes.
$$\text{Assessed Value} = \text{Market Value} \times \text{Assessment Rate}$$
The assessment rate is set by the local tax assessor.
$$\text{Property Tax} = \text{Assessed Value} \times \text{Tax Rate (decimal)}$$
Alternatively, if rate is in mills: $$\text{Tax} = \frac{\text{Assessed Value}}{1{,}000} \times \text{Mills}$$
Never use market value; always use assessed value.

What is a [[kw:mill]]?
back: 1 mill = $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.
Commonly used by local governments to express property tax rates.
To convert mills to decimal: divide by 1,000.
Mills = 25 mills.
All are equivalent.

Why is property tax based on assessed value rather than market value?
back: Assessment rates allow governments to adjust tax burdens without changing market values.
It can provide relief to homeowners by taxing only a fraction of market value.
Different property classes may have different assessment rates.
Sales tax is a general tax on most goods and services.
Excise tax is a specific tax on particular items (e.g., tobacco, alcohol, luxury goods).
Both are added to the retail price; excise tax is in addition to sales tax.
